description: Clean technology futures reproduce mineral sacrifice zones and land-intensive extraction.
AI platforms extract data labor and social knowledge while centralizing digital authority.
Climate stress is answered through borders surveillance military planning and resource control.
Development pathways are shaped by external finance technology and modernization metrics.
Conservation and carbon projects restrict land and livelihoods without community authority.
Reparative and decolonial futures are dismissed as unrealistic or destabilizing.
Public contestation expands the range of serious futures and shifts authority.
Future-making centers repair sovereignty ecological restoration and plural knowledge.
